newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, trade looks for leads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, trade looks for leads.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Thursday as players waited for the afternoon session to provide more leads for the market, dealers said.
"People are essentially waiting for leads this afternoon. The big boys are not in and there was no followthrough buying this morning," a dealer said.
The major consumers were not in the market a day after Bridgestone bought forward shipments of TSR20 grade rubber for around 109.00-111.00 U.S. cents a kg.
Prices were indicated higher in line with firmer prices in Tokyo, dealers said. The November contract in Tokyo rose 1.4 yen to 138.2.
"People were sitting on the sidelines. There was no offtake this morning," one dealer said.

At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 was indicated at 115.50 U.S. cents a kg from 114.50 cents. July RSS1 was indicated at 163.75-165.75 Singapore cents (US$1.14-$1.15) a kg from 163.75 cents. July TSR20 was indicated at 155.75-157.75 Singapore cents (US$1.09-$1.10) a kg from the previous 155.75 cents.
